questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to go to a place where the culture was different from Denmark but still familiar in the sense that it felt safe enough to wander alone and explore the city.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The city, culture, weather and food were amazing - I just had some personal issues which made it hard for me to enjoy the entire stay as I had hoped.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: The travel reports and KU were beneficial, the UAB (Spanish University) has a chaotic homepage mostly in spanish/catalan but are helpful if you write them an email.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I did not receive any assistance from the university. We had to go pay a fee upon arrival and it was quite hard to find the office to do so, given that the campus is huge and a lot of the people working there do not speak spanish... Could have been helpful with a more proper guide. Everything they did seemed to be the first time they did so.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: They seem unproffesional and new at receiving erasmus students.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I recommend to start searching early and perhaps if possible to find 3-4 other students to share an apartment in the Gracia, Eixample or El Born area. I was told it would be easy to find roommates once I arrived so I waited but it was not (as everybody already seemed to have found accomodation) so it was very stressfull in the end but I luckily ended up renting a room in the city center but with three much older strangers.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer:
Almost all the people who lived on campus regretted it as the train ride into Barcelona is almost an hour and there is no night trains if you wanna go clubbing etc. 
I honestly don't understand why one would wanna live on campus, the area is honestly a bit depressing and is far away from everything.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: If you prepare and read up on the courses, their exam dates, schedule and sit by the computer when they open for registration you will get the courses you want. BUT make sure they dont overlap, because it is your own problem and the uni are not that helpful (based on the other students stories).

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You have to check the language is OK, the mid terms, exams and schedules do not overlap which can take some time. But other than that I was happy it was digital as I had heard stories of people having to show up physically on the first day of school.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I don't believe there was much help and it was actually a bit difficult to find the updated schedule for all the courses so be careful you dont plan your courses after last year schedule - their homepage is a bit unclear.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all I wanted

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Just do your research in good time and make sure to get it accepted from KU and then you are good to go.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
As most of the other travel reports states: the university, the teachers and facilities is just on a much much lower level than what we are used to in KU. Most of the Erasmus students were in shock. 
They teachers change the "rules" of the course and currriculum as they please and all to feed their own ego. They treat students as they were in highschool and even mock students when they ask sincere question? We had one teacher yelling at us for one hour because she was so displeased with our level from the midterms - and afterwards when we received the grades, not a single student had failed?

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level is low. I had a teacher explain to the class of third year economics BA students what GDP consists of and everyone took notes. Eventhough the syllabus is much smaller and easier than what we are used to in Denmark it is still somewhat "difficult" to pass the midterms and exams as they teachers teach one thing and expect you to know another - it is very confusing. All the exams are btw hand written because they don't use computers.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The teachers are completely different and the spanish students do not respect them. The teacher is often late so as the students, and the teacher can often not get the students to be quiet. With that said they are all very different and some teachers were nice - however my overall experience is that their style of teaching is very confusing and they often say one thing and then do another.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: EU economic integration, Environmental economic, HR, Economic Policy, Foreign Trade

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Economic Policy and EU economic integration

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: It was more expensive to buy groceries and eat out than expected. But with that said you can live very cheap if you want to.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: It was mostly as I expected.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I cannot really say as I did not use any facilites offered by the UAB as I wanted to spend as little time on campus and as much time in the city.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: It may seem cringe but the Erasmus events are really helpful to meet new people and explore the city in the beginning. I met a lot of my friend there.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I recommend doing other stuff than the typical spanish - explore sunrise/sunset yoga at the beach, take a dancing class, go see drag shows, eat at the many korean restaurants, see some of the Gaudi houses on the inside, the Miro museum on Mont Juic is really nice, use the cinematique in El Born

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I really recommend going a bit outside of the city while the weather is good and go on the hiking trips such as Montserrat and explore one day trips to beaches in Sitges and Costa Brava. Erasmus also offer a lot of hiking in beautiful places, but I dont remember the names. GO!

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Easy

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Dont expect to - the spanish students keep to themselves and most of them do not speak english that well so it was really difficult. But enjoy all the other wonderful erasmus students!

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Spanish people are often late and they often don't do as they say. For example on more than one occassion professors, my landlord or the university office promised to do something/upload/send something at a specific time/before a date but never do - so you have to keep reminding them.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: People are much more approachable at cafes, streets, restaurants and the beach - especially in the summer. Everybody are just friendly, smilling, willing to talk and have a good time!

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Set your expectations low for the univeristy
2. Have your things in order, so you dont miss any deadlines
3. Dont be afraid to push the university by writing them emails if they forget you/respond late

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Just remember the university if about 50 min train ride back and forth so if you can schedule the courses so you have some days off you will appreciate it.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting so many many people from such different cultures and getting some very close friendships.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Finding a quiet spot in the city which wasn't crowded with people/tourist.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
